subtype: Direct gaze in interviews and dating [Regulating]
passage:
Dear Amandeep,
Thanks for the tips after my first internship interview. I told you eye contact makes my skin prickle. Since Tuesday I've tried what you suggested: looking at the eyebrows or the bridge of the nose, then glancing away at the notepad while I think. It felt less like a staring match. The panel didn't seem to mind. The interviewer even said I was a very good listener. But on a date on Friday, my usual steady gaze made the other person go quiet, which was odd, because I thought they'd like it. I've decided to soften it there too, glancing away when I laugh. It's a bit of a puzzle, but I'm getting there.
Chandrika

subtype: Direct gaze in interviews and dating [Regulating]
passage: Sarita, you asked how I handle interviews. Honestly, eye contact is hard for me. I'm Vijay, and when I look straight at someone, I lose track of what they're saying. So I usually look at their hands or a spot on the table. Early on, two interviewers decided I was uninterested. One said so afterwards. Now I tell them at the start: "I listen better when I'm not staring, so I'll glance away, but I'm following." I nod and repeat back their points, and that shows I am. The last panel said I answered more carefully than most. I do get tired after, but I've stopped thinking eye contact is the only way to show I care.

qa.q: What do the interviewers see Vijay looking at?
qa.a: Vijay usually looks at their hands or a spot on the table.

qa.q: What was Vijay feeling when the first interviewers judged Vijay uninterested?
qa.a: Vijay was probably frustrated and misunderstood, since Vijay was listening closely and simply finds direct eye contact hard.

qa.q: What does Vijay do now to help interviewers read Vijay fairly?
qa.a: Vijay tells them at the start about listening better while glancing away, then nods and repeats back their points to show attention.

qa.q: How might an interviewer who expects steady eye contact see Vijay at first?
qa.a: They might read the looking away as disinterest, so Vijay's explanation gives them a better way to understand Vijay.

grounding: A young adult who finds eye contact hard adjusts gaze and still listens well, since steady eye contact reads differently in different settings.
